recommendation: Keep the fix as-is. It resolves the semantic mismatch in the initial application and avoids a single root Availability.period that would not satisfy the approved per-availableTime period request.
issue_request: FHIR-41311 was an Applied/Persuasive PA change request asking for a period for each availability block and guidance about how that period relates to the containing resource period. The final resolution explicitly added Availability.availableTime.period 0..1 Period with display, definition, and comment text.
initial_application: Commit 52c81fc0778c00406004a8e1b68e22af65c97988, merged by PR #3040 in 2f6ff2fdb4d3b03836369a6e360571211c1dc5db, added the approved text to source/datatypes/availability.xml but named the row Availability.period. The row comment still referred to Availability.availableTime.period, showing the original application was at the wrong element level.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively maps availability to metadatatypes and lists Location, PractitionerRole, and HealthcareService as active resources consuming the datatype. PA minutes from 2023 discuss adding a period to Availability.availableTime, and 2024 WGM minutes record the 8-0-0 motion and the intended resource-period interaction. Bounded Jira/Zulip/Confluence searches found no later conflicting decision.
reconciliation: Moved the Period row under Availability.availableTime, renamed it Availability.availableTime.period, retained the approved 0..1 Period cardinality/type and display/definition/comment text, and ordered it with the availableTime children.
source_changes: source/datatypes/availability.xml: moved the approved Period row from Availability.period to Availability.availableTime.period and placed it immediately under the Availability.availableTime backbone element.
